issue_context.title: unexpected assertion failed using global index
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

<!-- a step by step guide for reproducing the bug. -->
Here is the log from our internal test schrddl. 
```
2024/10/09 16:48:19 ddl.go:212: [0;31m[fatal] [error] [instance 16] ERROR: Error 8141: assertion failed: key: 7480000000000000ba5f69800000000000000307800029e4698b0200, assertion: Exist, start_ts: 453113916671131764, existing start ts: 0, existing commit ts: 0
/build/ddl/dml_ops.go:52: Error when executing SQL: delete from `b5d472af` where not( IsNull( `b5d472af`.`56b0971e` ) ) or `b5d472af`.`56b0971e` in ( 1444517 ,824880 ) 
```

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)
No error
### 3. What did you see instead (Required)
assertion failed
### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)
master
<!-- Paste the output of SELECT tidb_version() -->
comments: Do DMLs during add global index (ingest mode) while trigger this problem

review_comments:
Is there always only a single index/element with IndexElementKey here?
What happens for `alter table t add index idx_1(b), add unique index idx_2(c) global`, where the indexes have different columns?
I'm not very familiar with the ingest add index code, but for non-ingest it will add all indexes in one go, one partition at a time. Is this the same for the mergingTmpIdx?

For multi-schema change, we will combine add indexes into one reorg job. So the elements will greatter than 1. This has nothing to do with whether it is a different column or not. See https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/47135 for details.

Ah, if there is any global index in elements, it will first do all global indexes by reading from the TableID, then it will do local indexes by looping over each partitionID and all the elements.

So do we also loop over all partitions even if there only are global indexes added?
